bifrost: springboard/src/shell/screentime/ (per-app limits, Downtime, allowed apps, Time Limit shield); springboard/src/shell/settings.rs (Screen Time pages). No app-facing SDK module.
summary: PermissionKit lets an app ask a child's parent or guardian for a communication or app-update exception through a system UI. BifrOSt has no app-facing equivalent: the system layer enforces Screen Time limits and Downtime, and no SDK module lets an app send a permission question to a parent or receive the answer.

features.feature: Creating a communication experience (AskCenter, PermissionQuestion, AskPermissionAction, AskError)
features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/permission_question.rs (PermissionQuestion, AskCenter::ask, AskError, PermissionButton); wired: springboard/src/shell/permission_sheet.rs (Sheet::new), springboard/sdk/src/permission_kit.rs
features.note: Question construction, the ask queue, expiry, the refusal of choices the question does not offer and the permission button are tested headless in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-tests-12.rs; the SDK re-exports the model, but no channel carries a question to a guardian, so an app cannot ask one yet, and AskPermissionAction has no counterpart in the model.

features.bifrost: springboard/ui/src/permission_question.rs (AskCenter::answer, AskCenter::take_responses, AskCenter::take_response, AskCenter::response_for); wired: springboard/src/shell/permission_sheet.rs (Sheet::finish reads the PermissionResponse from AskCenter::answer)
features.note: Answers are kept per topic in arrival order, read or taken once, as tested headless in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-tests-12.rs; the shell reads each answer as it arrives and does not drain the per-topic stream, and no channel returns a guardian's answer to an app asynchronously.

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 8 tests. Wave 4 (w4-permissionkit, parity/integration 0925691e): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on the VM or Midget. The shell can allow or block an app and grant a time-limit ignore for 15 minutes or the rest of the day. Parent approval of app updates is not implemented, and apps cannot request it.
Apple documents communication experiences as available only through iMessage. BifrOSt has no iMessage counterpart.

Per-app daily time limits and Downtime exist in the shell's Screen Time settings, tested headless in springboard/tests/parity_sdk-tests-10-w7.rs. They limit app use, not who a child may message, and there is no app-facing API for communication limits.

verified on Midget 0.7.25 by 16 tests. Wave 6 (b01, main): pure model with host unit tests; not wired into apps or the shell, not yet tested on Midget. The shield offers Ignore Limit, guarded by the Screen Time passcode, but it is a shell-only cover. No SDK button presents a parent request.

A custom topic routes its questions and answers by its name, as tested headless in springboard/ui/tests/parity_sdk-tests-12.rs; the topic is only a local name, and no protocol tells a guardian what an app is asking for.

gaps: No SDK API lets an app ask a parent or guardian for permission (AskCenter, PermissionQuestion, AskPermissionAction).
No asynchronous stream of parent responses (responses(for:), PermissionResponse) for apps.
No app-facing button or sheet that presents a parent-approval flow (PermissionButton).
Screen Time limits and Downtime are enforced by the shell but cannot be queried or requested by apps.
Parent approval of significant app updates (SignificantAppUpdateTopic) is not implemented.
